description:
**Files**:
- crate-jmap-chat-types/ — no FilterCondition, no Comparator (survey confirmed)
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs — \`type Filter = serde_json::Value;\` and \`type Comparator = serde_json::Value;\` on all 5 JmapObject impls (Chat, Message, Space, ContactCard analogue, etc.)

**Divergence**: every other extension type crate exposes at least one typed FilterCondition struct:
- mail-types: EmailFilterCondition, MailboxFilterCondition, EmailSubmissionFilterCondition
- calendars-types: CalendarFilterCondition, CalendarEventFilterCondition, NotificationFilterCondition
- tasks-types: TaskFilterCondition, TaskNotificationFilterCondition
- contacts-types: ContactCardFilterCondition
- filenode-types: FileNodeFilterCondition
- sharing-types: PrincipalFilterCondition, ShareNotificationFilterCondition
- metadata-types: MetadataFilterCondition

chat is the only extension whose query-filter shape is \`serde_json::Value\` at the type-system level.

**What goes wrong** (per AGENTS.md 'Filter algebra and control enums are explicitly EXCLUDED' / 'Silent-drop is a server-side query-correctness bug'):
1. Clients have no compile-time check that they're constructing a valid chat filter — typos in field names compile fine, fail at backend-decode time.
2. Backends can't dispatch on filter content via Rust pattern-matching; they have to interpret the JSON value or hand-roll a decoder.
3. The workspace's own correctness rationale (silent-drop produces wrong result sets with no error signal) applies to chat-server today: a query containing \`{"acmeUnknownClause": "x"}\` silently passes through chat-server's \`Value\` type and gets dropped on backend interpretation — exactly the failure mode AGENTS.md says the workspace must avoid.

**Mitigating context**: the JMAP Chat draft (\`draft-atwood-jmap-chat\`) may not yet specify the complete filter set for all 5 chat object types. \`Value\` may have been chosen as a placeholder pending spec maturity. If so, the right interim shape is still a typed struct with zero fields plus a serde \`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]\` so that filter clauses can be added one-by-one as the draft stabilizes, rather than \`serde_json::Value\`.

**Fix**: define typed (possibly empty) FilterCondition structs in chat-types for each of the 5 chat object types. Plain shape:
\`\`\`rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ChatFilterCondition {
    // populate from draft-atwood-jmap-chat as it stabilizes
    #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
\`\`\`
Then update chat-server's JmapObject impls to use \`type Filter = ChatFilterCondition;\` etc.

**Note**: even with \`extra: serde_json::Map\` for vendor-extension preservation, the typed struct still gives \`#[non_exhaustive]\` + named-field discoverability + compile-time safety for the spec-defined clauses as the draft adds them.
title: chat-types defines NO Filter/FilterCondition/Comparator types; chat-server backend uses `serde_json::Value` for all 5 object Filter/Comparator associated types
